original_card.question: Can a changed query demand or caller remove real work while satisfying native chronology and restoration?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose an exact caller and a new demand/interface hypothesis. Read the scoped #5617/#5631/#5649/#5747 and #5720/#5745 objections before rebuilding an excluded schedule. Compare the complete matched source/consumer protocols including all retained helper outputs. For an active-mode injection, first check #5745: its canonical delivery claim repays the eight removed centre jobs. Audit that exact claim or change its channel/feedback hypothesis; do not repeat the same free-injection search. Stop if the full favorable budget fails or the required restored output is unobservable.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.
allowed_variations: One exact source head, helper/cut region or quantified proposition and changed hypothesis; check live handoffs first. Different seeds are not different scopes.
scope_change_triggers: Changing source head, helper/cut domain, operation alphabet or caller boundary without recording the new scope.
Treating an archived proposal or local numerical pass as complete supplier admission.

actual_scope: Over F_2, every 4-by-4 matrix commuting with T has even (1+x)-valuation. The explicit idempotents E_11, E_22 and E_33+E_44 have valuations 1, 1 and 2 and their gates multiply to I+x I_4. The same nine gates multiply to the pure operator product_j (I+x_j E_j). The coefficient of e stays zero, and the selected frontier stays 781451/250000000.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a changed query demand removes real work. This package answers the open question left by PR #6956: whether a stage factor outside the T-commuting projectors can have (1+x)-valuation 1, so three factors can total valuation 4. The field, block size and leaf count stay F_2, d=2 and g=3. The 15,625-triple projector census is not rerun.
bottleneck_link: PR #6956 shows that three T-commuting projectors overshoot the pure determinant. A valuation-1 factor removes that count only outside the commutant. The witness meets the pure operator product_j (I+x_j E_j) and supplies neither a nilpotent factor nor a change to the selected frontier 781451/250000000.
stop_rule: Stop after the commutant square identity, the explicit triples, the exhaustive censuses of M_4(F_2), of the E_11 idempotent slice and of one non-idempotent slice, and the pure eight-dimensional product. Do not search thin maps, g=13, g=31, or a native bill.
evidence: verify.py checks the explicit products, all 256 commutant matrices, all 65536 matrices, all 802-by-802 idempotent pairs after E_11, all 65536 middle factors after one non-idempotent matrix, and the pure three-stage word. It prints PASS_PAIRED_STAR_VALUATION_ONE_FACTOR. Python 3.12, standard library only.

open_questions.question: Can a constant matrix R be inserted beside one exhibited factor so that the coefficient of e becomes I, while the pure product remains product_j (I+x_j E_j)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The coupled31 target is (I+e I) times that pure product. This package meets the pure product and leaves the coefficient of e equal to zero.
open_questions.first_step: Keep the exhibited diagonal gates. Expand (I+x E_11)(I+e R) on the stage-0 block and solve the linear equation for one constant R supported on that block.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing external. One rejected R is not a proof that none exists. This is not the unsplit full call E_j and it is not a g=13 or g=31 word.

open_questions.question: For a rank-1 idempotent other than E_11, are the idempotent triples that multiply to I+x I_4 exactly the orthogonal triples with third factor I+A+B?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The exhaustive idempotent classification in this package fixes the first factor as E_11. The orthogonal identity applies to every idempotent, and the other first factors are a separate finite census.
open_questions.first_step: Repeat the 802-by-802 idempotent multiplication for the rank-1 idempotent with rows (1, 1, 0, 0), and compare the hits with the idempotents orthogonal to it.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing external. The domain is finite. A second first factor would still leave non-idempotent triples unclassified.
